The CuTe-DSL/CUTLASS and CUDA versions used for the blog run are not stated and the per-size numbers exist only as a figure, so it stays C rather than A.

corrections.caveats: First-party blog numbers; the per-size results are only in a figure (combined_kernel_benchmarks_final.png); the text gives the 262k FP32 softmax ratio (3.01 vs 1.89 TB/s, which the blog calls 'nearly 50% more' though it is about 1.59x (derived from page data)) and the >=65k claim. Liger is only benchmarked up to reduction dim 65k (larger sizes unsupported) and cuDNN only on RMSNorm. Harness is public (benchmarks/benchmark_softmax.py, benchmark_rmsnorm.py, benchmark_cross_entropy.py) but has evolved since the July 2025 blog, and the blog does not state the CuTe-DSL or CUDA versions. Baselines are 2025 versions. Below about 4k reduction dim no advantage is claimed. It is a Python CuTe-DSL kernel library for PyTorch/JAX on H100/B200/RTX 50, not a C++ library.

notes: Blog text, README, repo page (Apache-2.0, 1.2k stars, not archived) and commits page (latest 2026-09-13) all match the record. Possible A if a later retier accepts PyTorch/Liger/cuDNN versions plus the public harness as sufficient, but the blog lacks the CuTe-DSL compiler version.

tier_reason: docs/benchmarks/m5.md gives the M3500 GN timings against GTSAM 4.2.1 (0.078 s vs 0.133 s in-sweep median of 5, 0.066 s vs 0.141 s standalone) with GCC 13.3 -O3, AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX, single-threaded, and the regeneration commands; the harness is public (bench/pgo2d_bench.cpp for sparsam, python/bench_m5_gtsam.py timing gtsam.GaussNewtonOptimizer.optimize() median-of-5) with raw CSVs committed.

corrections.baseline: GTSAM 4.2.1 (PyPI wheel driven through its Python bindings) on 2D pose graphs; Ceres 2.2 on BAL bundle adjustment
corrections.claimed_speedup: docs/benchmarks/m5.md: on M3500 (3500 poses) with both stacks converging to final chi-squared within 0.009%, sparsam GN (7 iterations) takes 0.078 s vs GTSAM GN (8 iterations) 0.133 s as in-sweep medians of 5, and 0.066 s vs 0.141 s standalone after cooldown; the author states the defensible claim as 1.7-2.1x faster end to end. Against Ceres 2.2 on BAL Ladybug (README), sparsam is slower in wall clock (1.74 s vs 0.67 s on ladybug-49, 1.57 vs 0.48 s on ladybug-73, 9.9 vs 4.9 s on ladybug-138, 26.5 vs 24.0 s on ladybug-318) but 552 vs 1091 ms per iteration on ladybug-318.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: GCC 13.3 -O3, single-threaded, Eigen 3.4.0 dense fixed-size kernels (docs/benchmarks/m4.md, m5.md); GTSAM side is the prebuilt gtsam==4.2.1 PyPI wheel (numpy<2), build flags not stated
corrections.caveats: Mixed result that the README itself states: Ceres wins wall clock on bundle adjustment (1.1-3.3x, mostly from fewer iterations), and on fill-heavy 3D pose graphs GTSAM's per-iteration linear algebra is about 3-5x faster than sparsam's simplicial block Cholesky. The M3500 speedup is end to end GN (7 vs 8 iterations), not a like-for-like factorization time, and the author notes laptop boost-clock state moves both numbers by about 15%. GTSAM was timed through its Python wheel (optimize() call only, median of 5) with wheel build flags unknown. sparsam's own LM plateaus on M3500 where GTSAM's LM converges. Author-run on one laptop; project created July 2026 with 1 star. Category fit is loose: a nonlinear least-squares/SLAM backend whose core is a from-scratch block-sparse Cholesky; baselines are GTSAM and Ceres, not SuiteSparse, Eigen sparse or PETSc.

notes: Numbers in the record match the README and m5.md; benchmark_url pointed at the repo root, corrected to m5.md. Repo page: MIT, 1 star, 0 forks, not archived; latest commit 2026-08-08, oldest visible 2026-07-18.

corrections.claimed_speedup: Peer-reviewed paper (Mastoras, Anagnostidis, Yzelman, 'Design and implementation for nonblocking execution in GraphBLAS: tradeoffs and performance', ACM TACO 20(1), 2023, doi 10.1145/3561652), per its abstract as quoted in search results: nonblocking execution reaches up to 16.1x over SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS and up to 12.2x over Eigen on ten matrices for the PageRank algorithm, and up to 4.11x (5.13x with the analytic model) over ALP's own blocking execution. Paper body not opened.
corrections.workload: PageRank on ten sparse matrices for the headline numbers against SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS and Eigen (per the abstract as quoted in search results); the paper reportedly also evaluates other algorithms such as conjugate gradient, which was not confirmed here. ALP/GraphBLAS nonblocking shared-memory backend.
corrections.caveats: Paper not opened (dl.acm.org, arxiv.org and researchgate.net are blocked from this container) and the ALP README contains no numbers, so matrices, CPU, thread counts, compiler, flags and the SuiteSparse:GraphBLAS/Eigen versions are unverified. The figures are 'up to' maxima for PageRank only; typical speedups and other algorithms are unknown. Gains come from fusing chained GraphBLAS primitives, so single-kernel speedups are likely smaller. The README dates the TACO paper 20(1), 2023 (the record said 2022).
